Every side the rules looked at

Six sides per game (both moneylines, both puck lines, over and under). EV is expected value at the DraftKings price using the probability the rules bet on: the no-vig DraftKings chance moved 30% toward the model. A bet needs +3% EV, a 45%+ chance, both ratings on the same side and confirmed goalies. Tags in grey are tests that log a pick with no stake.

Games and predicted scores

Every game tonight with a DraftKings line, plus the next 7 days from the schedule. The model’s numbers come from team expected-goal ratings (5-on-5, power play, penalty kill), the expected starting goalies, home ice and back-to-backs. Tap Show the math on any game.

Players to know (tonight’s projections)

Bias check

Standings and playoff odds

Real standings from the NHL, plus odds from 10,000 simulated seasons of the remaining schedule under the NHL’s rules: 2 points for a win, 1 for an overtime or shootout loss, top 3 in each division plus 2 wild cards per conference. Ties break on regulation wins, then regulation-plus-overtime wins, then wins (head-to-head isn’t simulated). MoneyPuck is a free second opinion from MoneyPuck’s own simulation.

Power ratings and tiers

Net is goals per game better than an average team on neutral ice, from expected goals (shot quality) at 5-on-5, on the power play and on the penalty kill, adjusted for each team’s usual starting goalie, weighted toward recent games and blended with last season early on. Results is the same idea from actual goals only, the second opinion the betting rules require to agree.

    Before trusting it, test it. Money stays off until the shadow bets earn the live switch. Closing line value (CLV) is the main test: if our bets keep getting better prices than where DraftKings closes, the model is finding something real long before a win–loss record can prove it.

    The model’s read on every game (logged before puck drop, never a bet) against the DraftKings no-vig line. Lower log loss is better; beating the market here is hard.
